summary: Event-ledger checkpoint + SIEM onboarding playbook for FluxPay payment events
description: Issue summary: FluxPay (enterprise) requests a reproducible onboarding playbook for delivering chronological, append-only audit events to their SIEM. They require: (1) per-hour checkpoints that provide an inclusion proof (Merkle-style) for a consumer to verify event continuity, (2) a field crosswalk for payment events to Splunk HEC and Sumo Logic, (3) automated gap detection + reconciliation guidance, and (4) example test payloads and a dry-run checklist.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer enabled 'audit-delta' export to their S3 bucket and configured the SFTP delivery hook; 2) Customer ran a small production load (payment auth and settlement flows) between 2026-03-08T22:00Z and 2026-03-09T04:00Z; 3) Customer observed that the SIEM ingestion showed non-chronological event timestamps and occasional duplicate event ids; 4) Customer requested ability to validate event continuity end-to-end and receive a signed checkpoint each hour.
logs:
Sample event (redacted): {timestamp: "2026-03-09T00:12:03Z", event_id: "evt_6f2a9", tenant_id: "fluxpay-01", type: "payment.auth", outcome: "approved", model: "rw-gen-13B"}
Delivery manifest excerpt: checkpoint_sha256: abc123...; s3_prefix: s3://fluxpay-audit/delta/2026-03-09/; manifest_signed_by: /CN=redwood-inference/signer
investigation_notes: Confirmed delivery path: audit-exporter -> S3 staging -> delivery-lambda -> customer SFTP. No TLS termination issues seen in logs.
Found occasional out-of-order events caused by our batching window when requests are routed to different serving pools; root cause: asynchronous flush of prefix cache for long-tail tenants.
Discovered duplicate event ids originate from at-least-once delivery path when retries occur during a brief SFTP 502 response from customer endpoint.
Customer requires a cryptographic checkpoint file per hour that contains a Merkle root and a signed sequence range to enable independent verification.
comments: 2026-03-11 Priya Reddy: Opening ticket with FluxPay request; provided initial template for field crosswalk and asked for sample event slices.
2026-03-11 Ethan Bauer: Assigned to infra-oncall; preliminary hypothesis: batching windows + retry semantics causing ordering/duplicate artifacts. Will assemble test harness.
2026-03-12 Miguel Santos (Customer): Sent three sample batches and SFTP server logs showing a 502 at 2026-03-09T01:17Z; asked whether signed checkpoints can be produced as GZIP manifest files.

2026-03-13 Ethan Bauer: Implemented a staging manifest that includes per-file sequence numbers and an hourly checkpoint generator (prototype). Shared dry-run checklist and Splunk HEC transformer snippets.
2026-03-13 Priya Reddy: Noted customer asked for a written 'gap reconciliation playbook' and a runbook entry for on-call to triage mismatch alerts.
resolution: Workaround and next steps: delivered a playbook draft and a prototype checkpoint generator to customer SFTP (hourly gzipped manifest + merkle_root.txt signed by Redwood's audit key). Recommended short-term config change: enable strict sequence numbering in audit-exporter to reduce out-of-order events. Long-term: schedule a Dedicated serving-runtime change to align flush windows across pools (RFC tracked in GH PR #628). Customer accepted the dry-run; next action: finalize signed checkpoint format and add automated reconciliation Lambda (task created for engineering).
